response: Menopausal hormone therapy (MHT) is known to sometimes cause irregular endometrial bleeding. Research suggests that uterine natural killer (uNK) cells may play a role in this phenomenon. uNK cells are a type of immune cell found in the uterus that help regulate menstrual bleeding and pregnancy. An imbalance or dysfunction of uNK cells may contribute to irregular bleeding in women taking MHT. Further study is needed to fully understand the relationship between uNK cells, MHT, and irregular endometrial bleeding.
